criteria: `parse_duration(text)` is added to `durations.py`.
`format_duration(seconds)` in `durations.py` stays as it is: `format_duration(5400)` gives `1h30m` and `format_duration(0)` gives `0s`.

`parse_duration(text)` returns the duration in whole seconds as an `int`; the text is one or more parts, where a part is a whole number followed directly by a unit: `h` (3600 seconds), `m` (60 seconds) or `s`; `1h30m` is 5400, `45s` is 45 and `2h` is 7200.
In `parse_duration`, a number is one or more of the digits `0`-`9`, it may be larger than the next unit holds and it may have leading zeros: `90m` is 5400, `05s` is 5 and `0s` is 0.
In `parse_duration`, units are lower-case: `1H` is invalid.
In `parse_duration`, parts come in the order hours, minutes, seconds, and no unit appears twice: `30m1h` and `1m2m` are invalid; a unit may be left out: `1h5s` is 3605.
In `parse_duration`, whitespace at the start and at the end of the text is ignored (`" 1h30m\n"` is 5400); whitespace anywhere else is invalid, as in `1h 30m` and `1 h`.

`parse_duration` raises `ValueError` for invalid text, including the empty string, text of only whitespace, a number with no unit (`1h30`), a unit with no number (`h`), an unknown unit (`10x`), a sign (`-5s`, `+5s`) and a fraction (`1.5h`).
`parse_duration` raises `TypeError` when its argument is not a `str`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
